articles.title: Goldman, Apollo seek buyers for $40 billion SpaceX AI chip deal
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management are in talks with investors to sell portions of a roughly $40 billion financing deal for SpaceX's AI chips, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday.

articles.title: CERT-In warns NBFCs and fintech firms of AI-driven attacks
articles.summary: An advisory from the government body said the AI-assisted financial threat is still active and warns BFSI entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.

articles.title: OpenAI, ready to IPO in 2027, now counts majority of sales from enterprises, Greg Brockman says
articles.summary: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on Wednesday the company now generates the majority of its revenue from enterprise sales and he believes it will be ready to go public in 2027.

articles.title: Wall Street Sees Risks to AI Boom After the Democratic Sweep
articles.summary: While stocks rallied as the Democratic sweep of Congress promises to exert a significant restraint on President Donald Trump, one key corner of the market was left out.
articles.author: Emily Forgash and Matthew Griffin

articles.title: Africa-Focused OPay Is Said to Halt US IPO After China Inquiry
articles.summary: Inquiries by a Chinese regulator prompted Nigeria-focused payments company OPay Ltd. to halt its $300 million US initial public offering just hours after setting the price, according to people familiar with the matter.
articles.author: Loni Prinsloo and Julia Fioretti

articles.title: Happiest Minds Q2 Revenue Rises 12.5%; AI Revenue Figure Remains Undisclosed
articles.summary: Happiest Minds reported a 12.5% revenue rise in Q2, with strong profit growth and ongoing merger plans with ITC Infotech.

articles.title: Google extends voluntary buyout offers to employees in several countries
articles.summary: The move comes amid mounting AI spending that has unnerved Wall Street and dented Alphabet's stock price. Microsoft last week offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees in an effort to contain costs. Alphabet's workforce has grown steadily in recent quarters, but it has sought to shift resources toward priority areas.

articles.title: Peppermint Robotics bags Rs 100 Cr in pre-Series B funding round
articles.summary: The startup, which makes autonomous cleaning robots, is backed by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners.

articles.title: AI Priority Shift Drives Market Reset: Morgan Stanley
articles.summary: Jitania Kandhari, deputy CIO of the solutions and multi-asset group at Morgan Stanley, discusses the ongoing correction in AI-related stocks, noting that investors’ priorities have shifted. "I think the markets are now saying not AI at any price, but AI with profit," Kandhari says on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: VC funding into Indian startups plunges 66% in October
articles.summary: The steep drop in venture capital funding into Indian startups has been primarily due to near absence of large value deals in the month of October.

articles.title: Wall Street CEOs, Big Money Managers Divided Over AI Risks
articles.summary: Some of the world’s biggest asset managers are sounding the alarm about risks to the artificial intelligence boom, even as Wall Street’s top CEOs talk up the potential windfall from the market.

articles.title: Morgan Stanley CEO Sees Up to $15T AI Investment Wave
articles.summary: Morgan Stanley Chairman and CEO Ted Pick suggests AI investment could reach $10 trillion to $15 trillion over the next decade, leveraging the potential of major productivity gains. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Most Venture Capital Is Going To Companies That Are Founded Or Led By Billionaires
articles.summary: More than half of all seed- through growth-stage venture capital raised in the U.S. so far in 2026 went to seven companies founded or led by men who are already billionaires. Together, these companies raised more than $260 billion in equity funding in the first 10 months of the year.
articles.author: Joanna Glasner

articles.title: Anthropic says revenue surged 1,100% ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly revenue and nearly $900 billion in spending commitments as it counts down to its Wall Street listing later this month. The filing said the company has committed to spend about $895 billion, mostly on computing power, with $70 billion of that due before September 2027.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs is pulling AI coding tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot from traders and bankers, limiting access to engineers only. As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti publicly praised "vibe coding" by non-technical staff. Now the bank cites "productivity and risk management" as the reason for the reversal. The article Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: Anthropic grows revenue twelvefold but posts $23 billion loss

articles.title: Anthropic Taps Macquarie, CommSec for Australia IPO Retail Offer
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC has tapped eight firms including Macquarie Group Ltd. and Commonwealth Bank of Australia’s CommSec unit for its Australian retail offer ahead of its highly anticipated Nasdaq debut that’s set to be among the largest ever initial public offerings.

articles.title: Oracle Kicks Off $20 Billion Capital Raise
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down debt offerings from Oracle, which is kicking off a $20 billion capital raise to finance its AI infrastructure spending, and Alphabet, which is tapping the European debt markets. Plus, Anthropic's revenue hits nearly $17 billion in the third quarter and Matt Witheiler, head of late-stage growth at Wellington and an Anthropic investor, joins to discuss new details from the amended IPO filing. And Apple is trading at its priciest level since 2008, ahead of its earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: NYC Comptroller Steps Up Criticism of Anthropic After IPO Filing
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC’s approach to its planned initial public offering threatens to disempower shareholders and prevent ordinary people from reining in a potentially dangerous form of technology, according to New York City’s comptroller.
